record_type_quote: We offer a conceptual replication, analyzing data on 560 children (males: 275) drawn from the NICHD Study of Early Child Care and Youth Development.

targets.authors: Hygen, B. W., Guzey, I. C., Belsky, J., Berg-Nielsen, T. S., Wichstrøm, L.
targets.title: Catechol-O-methyltransferase Val158Met genotype moderates the effect of disorganized attachment on social development in young children
targets.evidence_quote: It is important to appreciate that our focus on COMT should not be read to imply that only this polymorphism may play a moderating role vis-à-vis the effects of disorganization. Rather, we focused exclusively on this candidate gene because we conceptualized this inquiry from its inception as an attempt to test an intriguing and most original hypothesis and, thereby, conceptually replicate and extend the work of Hygen et al. (2014).
targets.outcome_quote: In any event, reasonably consistent support for the Norwegian hypothesis emerged in both inquiries as to why some children with disorganized attachment histories behave in seemingly controlling-caregiving and others in controlling-punitive ways.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors’ overall assessment supports the conceptual replication. Mother-only effects also match the original relationship specificity. They discuss differences in whether levels or change are predicted but conclude reasonably consistent support across both inquiries.

reasoning: Verified title and six authors. A different US cohort tests the specific Norwegian interaction; other cited attachment/genetic studies are background.
